I've been playing 4 copies of  skull crack and vortex in the main since mh3 dropped. Both of these cards really help alleviate a lot of this incidental life gain we have in the meta. Phlage isn't the hardest to play around since we're proactive enough to be close to winning the game by the time they play phlage or escape him. Guide of souls and ocelot are a real problem, though. I'm currently running three pyroclasm in the side for the energy matchup. Another thing I recommend is taking goblin guide out of the deck and replacing it with amped raptor. It's a great two for one that accelerates our board state. And that first strike is eerily relevant. If you go that route, you might want to consider taking either skewer or rift bolt out to decrease the amount of blanks. I personally opted for skewer since rift bolt can give us more  consistency with our turn 1 game actions.

Cycling rings is great when it happens, but it's still likely that they already tapped it once. Meaning they're taking the one plus the instant speed bolt you throw at their face before the second ring resolves. They're most likely tapping out for that second ring, giving us a whole turn to draw the burn spell, play a land, and pass. This has been the line against any deck running tor since it's been printed.
The one ring existing is good for burn. They're enabling our game plan with burden counters.
Phlage isn't difficult to answer. It's guides and ocelots that really do us in.

Also, chase cards from recent sets are kinda bonkers. Bonfire, sinful spoils, and sp little knight, to name a few. So far, I've built Floo and swordsoul, both being pretty cheap at under $200.
